gloss: to change color; to discolor; to fade

definitions.gloss: to change color; to discolor; to fade
definitions.explanation: For something to undergo a change in color, typically due to aging, chemical reaction, heat, or exposure to light. Usually implies an undesirable change.

examples.japanese: りんごが{変色|へんしょく}した。
{古|ふる}い{写真|しゃしん}が{変色|へんしょく}してしまった。
{切|き}ったアボカドは{空気|くうき}に{触|ふ}れると{変色|へんしょく}するので、レモン{汁|じる}をかけるとよい。
examples.english: Cut avocado discolors when exposed to air, so it helps to squeeze lemon juice on it.

notes:
Composed of {変|へん} (change) + {色|しょく} (color). Most commonly used for undesirable color changes — browning of food, fading of fabrics, yellowing of paper, or tarnishing of metals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {変色|へんしょく}を{防|ふせ}ぐ — to prevent discoloration
- {変色|へんしょく}した{部分|ぶぶん} — discolored area
- {熱|ねつ}で{変色|へんしょく}する — to discolor from heat
- {紫外線|しがいせん}で{変色|へんしょく}する — to discolor from UV light

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {色|いろ}が{変|か}わる — to change color; more casual and general, not necessarily negative
- {褪|あ}せる — to fade (of color); specifically about losing color intensity
- {黄|き}ばむ — to yellow, to turn yellowish; specific type of discoloration
